paper_metadata.title: High temperature phase transformation and mechanical properties of Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr high-entropy alloys formed by laser melting deposition (LMD)

evidence.quote: In this paper, a Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr refractory high-entropy alloy with lower density than equal atomic ratio alloy was formed by laser melting deposition technology, and its high temperature mechanical behavior and microstructure phase transformation behavior were systematically analyzed.
HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy was first proposed in 2011 and quickly gained widespread attention [8].
HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy system has the tendency of DRX at high temperature [31].

The Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr HEA ingots were firstly prepared by vacuum electromagnetic levitation melting technology and the raw materials were high-purity (≥99.9 %) Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti and Zr metals.

Using graphite dies, HEAs were remelted into Ø30mm × 250 mm cylindrical ingots which would be used for the next step of plasma rotation electrode process (PREP). Prepared HEA powder for LMD with a particle size of 30-150 μm (D10 = 45.23 μm, D50 = 72.38 μm, D90 = 116.4 μm) has good sphericity.
The LMD process was conducted using laser power of 1300 W, scanning rate of 270 mm/min, powder feeding rate of 8 g/min, and height increment of 0.35 mm of each layer.
The aging treatment temperature was 600 °C, 800 °C, 1000 °C, 1200 °C and 1400 °C for 24 h, and the microstructure was retained by water quenching.

evidence.quote: At 600 °C, only a single BCC phase was precipitated at the grain boundary and inside the grains of the alloy (Fig. 5a), and the phase was determined to be Zr and Hf-rich phase by energy spectrum analysis (Fig. 5g).

The BCC phase grows further at 800 °C, while the new HCP phase begins to precipitate (Fig. 5b). It is determined by the energy spectrum analysis result shown in Fig. 5h that the precipitated HCP phase is Zr and Ti-rich phase.

Further increasing the temperature to 1400 °C the precipitated phase appears again (Fig. 5f). Zr and Hf elements are enriched again (Fig. 5f), but different from the case at lower temperature, the enrichment of Zr and Hf elements is no longer precipitated in the form of BCC phase, but transformed into HCP phase.

The microstructure and lattice arrangement of the alloy at different temperatures were further analyzed by EBSD, and the statistics of the small-angle orientation difference inside the grains are shown in Fig. 6.

Nowadays, the most commonly accepted explanation for PLC mechanism is based on dynamic strain aging (DSA) model.

The serration behavior of the curve in the plastic deformation stage is the embodiment of the plastic instability deformation accompanied by dynamic strain aging during the stretching process. This phenomenon is found in the high temperature deformation process of various alloys and is summarized as the Portevin-Le Chatelier (PLC) effect [21].
